title: pvSegYReader
body:
## pvSegYReader

Reads a SEG-Y seismic file. 3-D surveys become a structured grid (default) or, with StructuredGrid false, a lighter image data whose positions and shape may be approximate; 2-D lines become a structured grid sheet. Axes are crossline, inline and depth, and the trace samples are the point values. Trace positions come from source, CDP or custom header bytes, and VerticalCRS decides whether the vertical axis is height (positive up) or depth.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The extended textual header is not read, so check VerticalCRS against the survey documentation.
- In Custom XYCoordMode set both XCoordByte and YCoordByte: ParaView's initial YCoordByte is 76, not the SEG-Y source-Y byte 77.
- Schemaxis generates this reader binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check with a sample file of this format.

Native constructor: `SegYReader`. Identity: `sources/SegY Reader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FileName` | This property specifies the file name for the SEG-Y reader. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Force2D` | Treats the file as a 2-D line even if it is a 3-D survey: the crossline and inline numbers are ignored and the traces are connected in file order into one structured-grid sheet through 3-D space. Use it for 2-D lines whose headers would otherwise be misread as 3-D. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `StructuredGrid` | Specify if we create a Structured Grid even when the data is SEG-Y 3D. Note this consumes more memory but it shows the precise location for each point and the correct shape of the data. The default value is true. If we set this option to false we create an Image Data for a SEG-Y 3D dataset. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `VerticalCRS` | Specify whether the vertical coordinates in the SEG-Y file are heights (positive up) or depths (positive down). By default, the vertical coordinates are treated as heights (i.e. positive up). This means that the Z-axis of the dataset goes from 0 (surface) to -ve depth (last sample). Note. As per the SEG-Y rev 2.0 specification, this information is defined in the Location Data Stanza of the Extended Textual Header. However, as of this revision, SegYReader does not support reading the extended textual header. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Heights","Depths"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Heights"` |
| `XCoordByte` | One-based byte position in each trace header from which the trace x coordinate is read when XYCoordMode is Custom (Source uses bytes 73/77, CDP 181/185). Use it for files that store coordinates at non-standard positions. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `XYCoordMode` | Specify whether to use source x/y coordinates or CDP coordinates or custom byte positions for data position in the SEG-Y trace header. Defaults to source x/y coordinates. As per SEG-Y rev 2.0 specification: - Source XY coordinate bytes = (73, 77) - CDP XY coordinate bytes = (181, 185) | `{"type":"enum","values":["Source","CDP","Custom"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Source"` |
| `YCoordByte` | One-based byte position in each trace header from which the trace y coordinate is read when XYCoordMode is Custom (Source uses bytes 73/77, CDP 181/185). | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvSegYReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
